chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the young girl who has not yet had her first menstruation and has not reached puberty, if a man buys her, he said: 'There is no waiting period (iddah) for her when he consummates the marriage.' And he said regarding a man who bought a girl, then freed her, and did not observe her waiting period (istibra'), he said: 'It was permissible for him to do so; if he did not do so, there is no blame upon him.'

key_terms.اِسْتَبْرَأَ رَحِمَهَا: observed waiting period to ensure purity from pregnancy

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a pre-pubescent slave girl upon marriage or manumission?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of 'iddeh' (waiting period) for pre-pubescent slave girls, establishing that consummation alone does not trigger a waiting period due to the absence of menstrual cycles. It further elucidates the principle of 'tanawul' (discretionary choice) in manumission, where the master is not penalized for failing to observe a waiting period if he chooses not to, reflecting the flexibility in early Islamic jurisprudence regarding slave status.
